boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Clark University
boards.description: Discover the essential late-night spots for Clark University students, from on-campus study hubs and cafes to local Worcester favorites that keep the campus fueled after dark.

cards.title: Higgins Late Night
cards.subtitle: Higgins University Center
cards.notes: Grab hand-tossed pizzas and hot subs at this student-favorite late-night service located within the Higgins University Center.
cards.short_summary: On-campus late-night dining service offering pizza and subs.
cards.evidence_claim: Higgins Late Night is open Thursday through Saturday from 9:00 p.m. to 2:30 a.m.
cards.source_title: Dining Services | Clark University
cards.access_notes: Open Thursday-Saturday until 2:30 a.m. during the academic semester.

cards.title: Freud's Coffee House
cards.subtitle: Higgins University Center
cards.notes: Enjoy espresso drinks and gourmet desserts at this cafe named after Sigmund Freud's historic 1909 visit to Clark.
cards.short_summary: Campus cafe serving espresso and desserts late into the night.
cards.evidence_claim: Freud's Coffee House is open Monday through Wednesday until midnight and Thursday through Saturday until 1:30 a.m.
cards.source_title: Dining Services | Clark University
cards.access_notes: Open until midnight Mon-Wed and 1:30 a.m. Thu-Sat.

cards.title: Academic Commons
cards.subtitle: Robert H. Goddard Library
cards.notes: Utilize this 24-hour study space for late-night projects and group work; a Clark ID is required for entry after 5 p.m.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour study space located within the Robert H. Goddard Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academic Commons is open 24 hours a day, with Clark ID required for entry after 5 p.m.
cards.source_title: Library Hours | Clark University
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours; Clark ID card required for access after 5:00 p.m.

cards.title: Wings Over Worcester
cards.subtitle: Main Street
cards.notes: Order crispy wings and tenders with over 15 signature sauces at this popular late-night delivery and pickup spot.
cards.short_summary: Local wing specialist known for late-night delivery near campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Wings Over Worcester is open until midnight or later on weekends for delivery and pickup.
cards.source_title: Wings Over Worcester
cards.access_notes: Open until 12:00 a.m. or later on Friday and Saturday nights.

cards.title: The Grind
cards.subtitle: Higgins University Center Basement
cards.notes: Visit this casual basement gathering space for student performances, events, and late-night socializing.
cards.short_summary: A student-run performance and social space in the University Center basement.
cards.evidence_claim: The Grind is a casual gathering space located on the ground floor (basement) of the Higgins University Center.
cards.source_title: Higgins University Center | Clark University
cards.access_notes: Hours vary by scheduled student events and programming.

cards.title: Dunkin' on Main
cards.subtitle: 1283 Main Street
cards.notes: Stop by for a late-night coffee or donut at this nearby location serving the Clark community.
cards.short_summary: A nearby Dunkin' location providing coffee and snacks to students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dunkin' at 1283 Main St serves the Worcester area near Clark University.
cards.source_title: Dunkin' 1283 Main St Worcester
cards.access_notes: Open daily; check specific evening hours for late-night availability.

cards.title: Acoustic Java
cards.subtitle: 932 Main Street
cards.notes: Visit this sustainable coffee roastery and cafe for organic food and specialty brews just steps from campus.
cards.short_summary: An independent coffee roaster and cafe located adjacent to Clark.
cards.evidence_claim: Acoustic Java is located at 932 Main St, Worcester, and offers specialty coffee and organic food.
cards.source_title: Location - Acoustic Java
cards.access_notes: Open daily; typically closes in the early evening.

cards.title: Belén's Clark Brunch
cards.subtitle: Main Street
cards.notes: Dine at this historic spot formerly known as Annie's, now serving a fusion of American diner classics and Salvadoran dishes.
cards.short_summary: A legendary campus-adjacent diner serving brunch and Salvadoran fusion.
cards.evidence_claim: Belén's Clark Brunch opened in the former Annie's Clark Brunch space on Main Street in 2026.
cards.source_title: Belén's Clark Brunch to open | ClarkU News
cards.access_notes: Check seasonal hours for late-morning and afternoon service.

cards.title: The Bistro
cards.subtitle: Higgins University Center
cards.notes: Meet friends for burgers, fries, and smoothies at this casual dining hub located on the ground floor of the UC.
cards.short_summary: A casual on-campus dining spot with multiple food platforms.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bistro is open daily until 9:00 p.m. for casual dining.
cards.source_title: The Bistro | Clark University
cards.access_notes: Open until 9:00 p.m. seven days a week.

cards.title: Pepe's Taqueria
cards.subtitle: Chandler Street
cards.notes: Order authentic Mexican burritos and tacos from this local favorite, known for its family recipes and generous portions.
cards.short_summary: A local Mexican restaurant popular for delivery to the Clark campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Pepe's Taqueria is open until 9:00 p.m. on Friday and Saturday.
cards.source_title: Pepe's Taqueria
cards.access_notes: Open until 9:00 p.m. on weekends; closed Sundays.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Discover the functional study hubs, quiet retreats, and specialized resource centers that define daily life for Clarkies beyond the standard admissions path.

cards.title: The Academic Commons
cards.subtitle: First Floor of Goddard Library
cards.notes: Head to the first floor for a high-energy group study environment. It is the primary spot for collaborative projects and houses the ITS Help Desk for tech support.
cards.short_summary: A bustling first-floor hub in Goddard Library designed for group work and social studying.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academic Commons on the first floor is described as a bustling area for group study or catching up with friends.
cards.source_title: Goddard Library | Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Open during standard library hours; accessible to all students with a Clark ID.

cards.title: The Grind
cards.subtitle: Higgins University Center Basement
cards.notes: Visit this basement-level casual gathering space for a break from the library. It often hosts small performances and serves as a relaxed alternative to the main dining hall.
cards.short_summary: A casual basement gathering space in the Higgins University Center used for relaxation and events.
cards.evidence_claim: The Grind is located on the ground floor (basement) of the Higgins University Center as a casual gathering space.
cards.source_title: Higgins University Center | Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Located in the basement of the UC; typically open late for student use.

cards.title: Media Arts Study Hub (MASH)
cards.subtitle: Traina Center for the Arts
cards.notes: Utilize this open study space on the second floor of Traina. It features modern and legacy tech, plus the university's extensive media collections for research.
cards.short_summary: A specialized study hub in the Traina Center equipped with media collections and technology.
cards.evidence_claim: The MASH is an open study space on the second floor of the Traina Center for the Arts equipped with modern and legacy technology.
cards.source_title: Media Arts Study Hub (MASH) | Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Open to students; specifically serves Visual and Performing Arts but available for general study.

cards.title: Kasperson Research Library
cards.subtitle: Woodland Street
cards.notes: Walk to Woodland Street for one of the quietest spots on campus. This library specializes in environmental research and offers a focused, low-distraction atmosphere.
cards.short_summary: A quiet, specialized research library located a short walk from the main campus center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Jeanne X. Kasperson Research Library supports environmental research and is noted as an extremely quiet 'hidden gem' for study.
cards.source_title: Jeanne X. Kasperson Research Library | Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Located at 931 Main Street/Woodland Street; check specific hours for research access.

cards.title: Lasry Center Lounges
cards.subtitle: Lasry Center for Bioscience
cards.notes: Take advantage of the natural light in these modern lounge spaces. They are ideal for science students between labs or anyone seeking a bright, quiet place to read.
cards.short_summary: Modern, light-filled lounge areas within the LEED Gold certified bioscience building.
cards.evidence_claim: The Lasry Center for Bioscience features lounge spaces with an abundance of natural light for teaching and collaborative work.
cards.source_title: Lasry Center for BioScience | Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Accessible during building hours; primarily used by science students but open to all.

cards.entity_name: Dana Commons Prayer and Meditation Room
cards.title: Dana Commons Quiet Room
cards.subtitle: Dana Commons
cards.notes: Find a moment of silence in the prayer and meditation room. This space is dedicated to reflection and provides a peaceful break from the academic grind.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated quiet space for prayer and meditation located within the Dana Commons hub.
cards.evidence_claim: Students can use Dana Commons for various activities, including the prayer and meditation room.
cards.source_title: Dana Commons | Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Open to all students seeking a quiet space for reflection or prayer.

cards.title: The Zen Garden
cards.subtitle: Outside Estabrook Hall
cards.notes: Study outdoors in this landscaped garden between Estabrook and the Little Center. It features benches and a peaceful atmosphere for fair-weather reading.
cards.short_summary: A tranquil outdoor garden space perfect for quiet study and fresh air.
cards.evidence_claim: The Zen Garden is located just outside Estabrook and the Little Center and is described as a beautiful place to study.
cards.source_title: 5 Best Places to Study on Clark's Campus
cards.access_notes: Public outdoor space; best used during daylight hours.

cards.title: Rose Library
cards.subtitle: Cohen-Lasry House
cards.notes: Visit this specialized library within the Strassler Center for a scholarly, quiet environment. It houses a unique collection focused on Holocaust and genocide studies.
cards.short_summary: An intimate and quiet research library located in the historic Cohen-Lasry House.
cards.evidence_claim: The Rose Library is part of the Strassler Center for Holocaust and Genocide Studies and holds a specialized collection.
cards.source_title: Rose Library | Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Check Strassler Center hours for public access; typically quiet and focused.

cards.title: The Craft Studio
cards.subtitle: Higgins University Center Basement
cards.notes: Get creative in this basement studio. It is a dedicated space for students to work on hands-on projects and artistic endeavors outside of formal classes.
cards.short_summary: A student-accessible studio for arts and crafts located in the University Center basement.
cards.evidence_claim: The Craft Studio is located in the basement level of the Higgins University Center.
cards.source_title: Higgins University Center | Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Available for student use; check with the Information Desk for supply access.

cards.title: Fifth Floor Silent Carrels
cards.subtitle: Top Floor of Goddard Library
cards.notes: Seek out the fifth-floor carrels for absolute silence. These individual desks near the windows offer views of Downing Street and the most focused environment in the library.
cards.short_summary: The highest level of Goddard Library, offering individual carrels for silent, deep work.
cards.evidence_claim: The fifth floor of Goddard Library contains reading carrels for general use, including those closest to Downing Street.
cards.source_title: Facilities | Robert H. Goddard Library
cards.access_notes: Silent study floor; individual carrels are first-come, first-served.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Discover free social spaces and activities at Clark University, from art galleries and nature trails to student-only fitness access and late-night lounges.

cards.title: Hike the Hadwen Arboretum
cards.subtitle: 26-acre woodland green space
cards.notes: Explore 26 acres of trails and heritage trees just a 15-minute walk from campus. It is open to the public daily for hiking and nature study at no cost.
cards.short_summary: A university-owned 26-acre woodland featuring hiking trails and over 66 species of trees.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hadwen Arboretum is Clark University's 26-acre public green space... containing 26 acres of woodland green space... open to the public all year.
cards.source_title: Home | Hadwen Arboretum | Clark University
cards.access_notes: Open daily from dawn to dusk for public use.

cards.title: View Art at Schiltkamp Gallery
cards.subtitle: Professional and student art exhibitions
cards.notes: Visit the Traina Center to see rotating contemporary art exhibitions. Admission is free for students and the public during regular gallery hours.
cards.short_summary: The main gallery space at Clark University hosting professional and student art exhibitions.
cards.evidence_claim: The Jacob and Alida Hoven Schiltkamp Gallery is Clark University's main gallery space... Admission free.
cards.source_title: Schiltkamp Gallery | Department of Visual and Performing Arts - Clark University
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Thursday 9 a.m.-9 p.m., Friday 9 a.m.-4:30 p.m., and weekends 12 p.m.-5 p.m.

cards.title: Browse the Leisure Reads Collection
cards.subtitle: Popular fiction and non-fiction
cards.notes: Head to Room 209 to find popular books for recreational reading. Students can borrow titles for free using their Clark OneCard.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated section of the main library for recreational reading materials available to students.
cards.evidence_claim: Relax with a popular fiction or nonfiction title. New books are added throughout the year. Browse the shelves by Room 209.
cards.source_title: Student Services | Robert H. Goddard Library | Clark University
cards.access_notes: Open until midnight most nights during the academic year.

cards.title: Work Out at the Kneller
cards.subtitle: Student gym and cardio facilities
cards.notes: Access cardio and weight equipment at the Kneller Athletic Center. Entry is free for all current students with a valid Clark OneCard.
cards.short_summary: The primary fitness facility for Clark University students located within the Kneller Athletic Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Use of Clark University athletic and recreational facilities is reserved for our students... Use requires a valid Clark ID.
cards.source_title: Facility Policies and Procedures - Clark University - Clark Athletics
cards.access_notes: Requires valid Clark ID for entry; check seasonal hours on the athletics website.

cards.title: Relax at University Park
cards.subtitle: Public park across from campus
cards.notes: Walk across Main Street to enjoy this public park featuring Crystal Pond, basketball courts, and open green space for social gatherings.
cards.short_summary: A historic 13-acre public park located directly across from Clark University's main entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: University Park... Anchored by Crystal Pond, the park is perfect for year-round use, hosting basketball and volleyball courts.
cards.source_title: Worcester Parks for Enterprising Clarkies - The Scarlet
cards.access_notes: Public city park open daily from dawn to dusk.

cards.title: Hang Out at The Bistro
cards.subtitle: Casual student social hub
cards.notes: Meet friends in the spacious seating area of the Higgins University Center. No purchase is required to use the lounge for socializing or studying.
cards.short_summary: A casual dining and social space in the Higgins University Center known for its relaxing atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bistro features four dining platforms and a spacious, relaxing atmosphere... a convenient place to meet your friends.
cards.source_title: The Bistro | Campus Map - Clark University
cards.access_notes: Open late for student use; check current dining hours for food service times.

cards.title: Attend a Theater Production
cards.subtitle: Student-led stage performances
cards.notes: Watch live theater productions in the Little Center. Tickets are typically free for students with a valid Clark ID, though reservations are required.
cards.short_summary: A black box theater hosting Visual and Performing Arts Department productions.
cards.evidence_claim: Tickets are $5 or free with a valid Clark ID. All tickets (even free ones) must be reserved.
cards.source_title: V&PA presents Molière's Tartuffe | Events - Clark University
cards.access_notes: Performance times vary; check the university events calendar for the current schedule.

cards.title: Gather in Red Square
cards.subtitle: Central campus plaza
cards.notes: Visit the brick plaza between Jonas Clark Hall and the library for free outdoor events, club tabling, and community festivals throughout the year.
cards.short_summary: The central outdoor gathering space on campus for student activities and university events.
cards.evidence_claim: Join us in Red Square for our Welcome Home celebration... Red Fair in Red Square... Career Festival.
cards.source_title: Events - Clark University
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 as a public campus thoroughfare.

cards.title: Swim at the Kneller Pool
cards.subtitle: Indoor recreational swimming
cards.notes: Take advantage of free open swim hours at the university pool. Access is included for all students with their Clark OneCard.
cards.short_summary: An indoor swimming facility available for recreational use by the Clark University community.
cards.evidence_claim: The multipurpose Kneller Athletic Center... includes a swimming pool... To use the facility, you must have a valid Clark ID.
cards.source_title: Health and wellness | Clark University
cards.access_notes: Check the athletics website for specific open swim and lap swim hours.

cards.title: Ride the WRTA for Free
cards.subtitle: City-wide bus transportation
cards.notes: Use the Worcester Regional Transit Authority buses to explore the city without paying a fare. The system is currently fare-free for all riders through June 2025.
cards.short_summary: Public bus transportation serving the Worcester area, currently operating without fares.
cards.evidence_claim: Worcester Regional Transit Authority buses... are currently fare-free through June 2025.
cards.source_title: 10 things to know for fall 2024 | ClarkU News
cards.access_notes: Buses run daily; check WRTA schedules for specific route times from the Main Street stops.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Choose ten distinct study environments. Verify access rules, room or reservation constraints, and the physical affordance that makes each useful.

cards.title: The 24-Hour Hub
cards.subtitle: Goddard Library, Plaza Level
cards.notes: Access this bustling group study area 24/7 with your Clark OneCard. It features the ITS Help Desk, Jazzman's Café, and plenty of collaborative table space.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour collaborative study hub on the plaza level of Goddard Library featuring a café and tech support.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academic Commons is open 24 hours a day, Clark ID is required for entry after 5 p.m.
cards.source_title: Library hours | Robert H. Goddard Library
cards.access_notes: Open 24 hours for students with OneCard; public access 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.

cards.title: Quiet Reading Carrels
cards.subtitle: Goddard Library, 5th Floor
cards.notes: Find deep focus in the reading carrels overlooking Downing Street. This floor is designated for quiet study and includes six general-use computer workstations.
cards.short_summary: Quiet individual study carrels and computer stations located on the top floor of Goddard Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The fifth floor has reading carrels closest to Downing Street for general use and is a quiet study floor.
cards.source_title: Find Tech Spaces | Information Technology Services
cards.access_notes: Accessible during standard library hours; typically 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. for the public.

cards.title: The Multimedia Lounge
cards.subtitle: Traina Center for the Arts, 2nd Floor
cards.notes: Study among media collections in this open space. It is equipped with modern and legacy tech, including Blu-ray and archival film stations for VPA students.
cards.short_summary: A specialized study space in the Traina Center featuring media collections and legacy technology stations.
cards.evidence_claim: The MASH is an open study space equipped with a wide array of modern and legacy technology on the second floor of Traina.
cards.source_title: Media Arts Study Hub | Department of Visual and Performing Arts
cards.access_notes: Open Monday-Friday 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. and Saturday noon to 5 p.m.

cards.title: Modern Main Street Study
cards.subtitle: Alumni and Student Engagement Center
cards.notes: Utilize the modern lounge spaces in Clark's newest facility. Grab a drink from the first-floor coffee shop and find a seat in the bright, open atrium.
cards.short_summary: A modern, sunlit lounge and study area located in the Alumni and Student Engagement Center.
cards.evidence_claim: ASEC provides a new, modern atmosphere with plenty of lounging space that is perfect for studying.
cards.source_title: Shaich Family Alumni and Student Engagement Center (ASEC) | Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Card access 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. daily; unlocked during Campus Store hours.

cards.title: Casual Dining & Study
cards.subtitle: Higgins University Center, 1st Floor
cards.notes: This casual dining hub offers a spacious atmosphere for informal study sessions. It is a popular spot for meeting friends between classes.
cards.short_summary: A casual dining area in the University Center that doubles as a social study space.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bistro features four dining platforms and a spacious, relaxing atmosphere convenient for meeting friends.
cards.source_title: The Bistro | Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Building open 7 a.m. to midnight; card access required after 7 p.m.

cards.title: The Skylit Science Lounge
cards.subtitle: Lasry Center for Bioscience
cards.notes: Study in a LEED Gold-certified environment. The three-story, skylit atrium provides informal lounge spaces with abundant natural light for science students.
cards.short_summary: A bright, three-story atrium in the bioscience center designed for informal study and interaction.
cards.evidence_claim: The building interior is organized around a three-story, skylit atrium that provides space for informal interaction.
cards.source_title: Lasry Center for BioScience | Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Card access 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. Monday through Sunday.

cards.title: Collaborative Reservable Rooms
cards.subtitle: Goddard Library, Multiple Floors
cards.notes: Book a private room for up to two hours via LibCal. Rooms range from individual carrels to group spaces equipped with plasma displays for presentations.
cards.short_summary: Reservable private rooms in Goddard Library for individual or group academic work.
cards.evidence_claim: Student study spaces may be reserved for up to two hours and renewed for an additional two hours daily.
cards.source_title: Facilities | Robert H. Goddard Library
cards.access_notes: Reservations required via Clark LibCal; keys must be checked out at the service desk.

cards.title: The Business Hub
cards.subtitle: Carlson Hall, School of Business
cards.notes: A dedicated space for School of Business students to collaborate. This historic building features modern classrooms and lounge areas for management majors.
cards.short_summary: Study lounges and collaborative spaces located within the Clark University School of Business.
cards.evidence_claim: Carlson Hall is home to the Clark University School of Business and features classrooms and lounge areas.
cards.source_title: Carlson Hall | Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Card access 7:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Friday.

cards.title: The Research Corridor
cards.subtitle: Sackler Sciences Center
cards.notes: When not in use for classes, the seminar rooms in Sackler offer quiet, professional environments for science and math students to work on research.
cards.short_summary: Seminar and research rooms in the science center available for student study between classes.
cards.evidence_claim: Sackler Sciences Center offers more than 50,000 square feet of research and teaching laboratories, lecture and seminar rooms.
cards.source_title: Arthur M. Sackler Sciences Center | Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Card access 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. Monday through Sunday.

cards.title: The Social Sciences Nook
cards.subtitle: Jefferson Academic Center
cards.notes: Located near the Geography and History departments, this building offers quiet corners and high-performance computing labs for social science research.
cards.short_summary: Study areas and computer labs within the historic Jefferson Academic Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Jefferson Academic Center maintains high-performance computing environments for teaching and research.
cards.source_title: Jefferson Academic Center | Campus Map
cards.access_notes: Card access 7 a.m. to 11 p.m. Monday through Sunday.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each

cards.subtitle: Main South Corridor
cards.notes: Visit this local diner for Salvadoran-inspired brunch and pupusas in the historic space formerly known as Annie's.
cards.short_summary: A neighborhood diner on Main Street serving a blend of American breakfast and Salvadoran specialties.
cards.evidence_claim: Belén’s Clark Brunch opened at 934 Main St., taking over the longtime home of Annie’s Clark Brunch near Clark University.
cards.source_title: New diner opens in longtime Annie's Clark Brunch location on Main Street
cards.access_notes: Open for breakfast and lunch; check current hours for specific brunch service times.

cards.title: Main Street
cards.subtitle: Main South Corridor
cards.notes: Walk across the street to 'Crystal Park' to enjoy the walking trails, basketball courts, and views of Crystal Pond.

cards.title: Park Avenue

cards.evidence_claim: Peppercorn's is located on Park Avenue near Clark University and Downtown Worcester.

cards.title: Beaver Street

cards.short_summary: A multi-use athletic facility on Beaver Street supporting Clark's varsity teams and recreation.

cards.access_notes: Private residence; viewable from the public sidewalk on Woodland Street.

cards.title: Maywood Street
cards.subtitle: Campus Gateway
cards.notes: Start your campus journey at the Bassett Admissions Center, located in a converted Victorian house on Maywood.
cards.short_summary: The primary entry point for prospective students, located at the corner of Maywood and Main.
cards.evidence_claim: The Undergraduate Admissions Office is located at 1 Maywood Street.
cards.source_title: Our campus and location - Clark University
cards.access_notes: Open during standard business hours for prospective students and visitors.

cards.title: Downing Street
cards.subtitle: Campus Pedestrian Plaza
cards.notes: Access the campus pool, gym, and racquetball courts at this central athletic hub on Downing Street.
cards.short_summary: Clark's main athletic facility featuring a swimming pool, gymnasium, and fitness center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Kneller Athletic Center is located on Downing Street and houses the university's main athletic facilities.

cards.short_summary: A key residential street in the Main South neighborhood frequently used for off-campus student housing.
cards.evidence_claim: Charlotte Street is listed as a nearby street for off-campus housing options for Clark students.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: From the surprise cancellation of classes on Spree Day to the historic lectures of Sigmund Freud, Clark University's traditions blend academic rigor with spirited community rituals.

cards.title: The Ultimate Surprise Day Off
cards.subtitle: A Century-Old Spring Tradition
cards.notes: Wake up to a surprise email canceling all classes for a day of inflatables, food trucks, and music on the Green.
cards.short_summary: Spree Day is a surprise holiday where classes are canceled for a day of campus-wide festivities and relaxation.
cards.evidence_claim: Spree Day is an evolving event since 1903 where Clarkies let loose when classes are canceled one day each spring.
cards.source_title: Annual events | Clark University
cards.access_notes: Occurs annually on a surprise weekday during the spring semester; open to all students.

cards.title: A Global Showcase in the Kneller
cards.subtitle: Flag Ceremony and Cultural Performance
cards.notes: Watch over 300 students perform traditional dances and music, culminating in a massive flag ceremony representing global home countries.
cards.short_summary: The International Gala is Clark's largest student-run event, featuring a variety showcase of global cultures and a grand flag ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: International Gala is a variety showcase of traditional and contemporary dance, music, theater, and fashion from many cultures.
cards.source_title: Traditions | Student Leadership, Identity, and Community Engagement | Clark University
cards.access_notes: Held annually in the spring at the Kneller Athletic Center; tickets are typically required.

cards.title: Breakfast Served by Professors
cards.subtitle: Finals Week Fuel at Higgins
cards.notes: Head to Higgins Dining Hall during finals week to be served a late-night meal by university staff and administrators.
cards.short_summary: Late Night Breakfast is a finals week tradition where staff and administrators serve students a free late-night meal.
cards.evidence_claim: Late Night Breakfast is a long-standing tradition where Clark staff and administrators serve students a late-night meal in Higgins Dining Hall.
cards.source_title: Traditions | Student Leadership, Identity, and Community Engagement | Clark University
cards.access_notes: Held late at night during finals week; free for all students with a valid Clark ID.

cards.title: The Scholarly Side of Spree
cards.subtitle: Undergraduate Research Festival
cards.notes: Present your original research or creative work alongside faculty mentors during this annual spring academic festival.
cards.short_summary: Academic Spree Day (now part of ClarkFEST) is a tradition where undergraduates present their research and creative projects.
cards.evidence_claim: Academic Spree Day celebrates student work produced under the mentorship of the University's distinguished faculty during the academic year.
cards.source_title: Clark University Academic Spree Day, Fall Fest and ClarkFEST | Student Works
cards.access_notes: Held annually in the spring, typically in the Higgins University Center.

cards.title: The Secret Backup Plan
cards.subtitle: A Campus Architectural Legend
cards.notes: Listen to the urban legend that Jonas Clark Hall was designed to be converted into a factory if the university failed.
cards.short_summary: The Jonas Clark Hall Factory Myth is a persistent campus legend about the building's industrial-style architectural design.
cards.evidence_claim: There exists a rumor that Jonas Clark had planned that, in the event that the University failed, he would turn the building into a factory.
cards.source_title: Do you know these Clark rumors and legends? - The Scarlet
cards.access_notes: The building is open during academic hours; the myth is a staple of campus tours.

cards.title: The Only U.S. Lecture
cards.subtitle: Commemorating the 1909 Visit
cards.notes: Visit the statue of Sigmund Freud, marking the only American university where the founder of psychoanalysis ever lectured.
cards.short_summary: The Sigmund Freud statue commemorates his historic 1909 visit to Clark, the only place in the U.S. where he gave lectures.
cards.evidence_claim: Sigmund Freud's only trip to America was to Clark's 1909 conference where he delivered five lectures.
cards.source_title: Photo Essay: Clark's Sigmund Freud statue | ClarkU News
cards.access_notes: Located on the campus green (Red Square) and accessible to the public 24/7.

cards.title: A Defiant Student Voice
cards.subtitle: Renamed During the Red Scare
cards.notes: Read the student newspaper, renamed in 1939 despite administrative concerns during the 'red scare' era.
cards.short_summary: The Scarlet is Clark's student-run newspaper, known for its independent editorial history and historic name change.
cards.evidence_claim: Renaming the paper to The Scarlet in 1939 was not favored by the administration because of the ongoing 'red scare' of communism.
cards.source_title: Clark News becomes The Scarlet, 1939
cards.access_notes: Available online and in print at the University Center and Goddard Library.

cards.title: Faculty as Your Waiters
cards.subtitle: A Nostalgic Senior Week Meal
cards.notes: Enjoy a final meal in the dining hall where faculty and staff volunteer to serve as your waitstaff during Senior Week.
cards.short_summary: Senior Brunch is a tradition where graduating seniors are served a meal by university faculty and administrators.
cards.evidence_claim: One tradition is the Senior Brunch, where faculty, staff and administrators volunteer to serve as wait staff.
cards.source_title: Senior Toast and Brunch help celebrate a time in between | ClarkU News
cards.access_notes: Held annually in May for graduating seniors; typically takes place in the Higgins Dining Hall.

cards.title: The Green That Is Red
cards.subtitle: The Heart of Campus Life
cards.notes: Gather at 'Red Square,' the central campus green named for the surrounding red-brick architecture rather than its actual color.
cards.short_summary: Red Square is the central meeting space on campus, ironically named despite being a grassy green area.
cards.evidence_claim: Clark's Campus Square, known by students, faculty, and staff as 'Red Square,' is home to many activities.
cards.source_title: Neighborhood | University Park Partnership
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible outdoor space at the center of the university campus.

cards.title: Late Night Laughs
cards.subtitle: Clark's Oldest Improv Group
cards.notes: Catch a high-energy performance by the Peapod Squad, Clark's long-standing student improv comedy troupe.
cards.short_summary: The Peapod Squad is a beloved student improv group that has been a staple of campus entertainment for decades.
cards.evidence_claim: Peapod Squad and Shenanigans! come together... Clark University puts a truly amazing effort into giving its students a wide variety of activities.
cards.source_title: The Scarlet - Volume XCII, No. 15 (March 21, 2013) - Clark Digital Commons
cards.access_notes: Performances typically held in Atwood Hall or The Grind; check student event calendars for dates.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Clark University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A guide for new Clarkies to navigate their first few days on campus, from essential dining spots to local green spaces and campus traditions.

cards.title: Move-In and Meet Your Peer Mentor
cards.subtitle: Friday Morning Arrival
cards.notes: Check into your residence hall and meet your Peer Mentor. They help you navigate the First-Year Experience and introduce you to your floor community.
cards.short_summary: The official start of your Clark journey begins with residence hall check-in and meeting your student mentors.
cards.evidence_claim: Orientation provides a time for First Year Students to move into residence halls and meet your peer mentor before the start of classes.
cards.source_title: Orientation for First Years | Events - Clark University
cards.access_notes: Access is restricted to students with valid housing assignments and their families during move-in hours.

cards.title: First Meal at the Higgins Cafe
cards.subtitle: Friday Lunch
cards.notes: Visit the flagship dining hall for an all-you-care-to-eat meal. It features brick oven pizza, vegan options, and international cuisines.
cards.short_summary: The primary campus dining hall offering diverse food stations and a central social hub for students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Table at Higgins is the flagship campus dining experience, featuring an all-you-care-to-eat selection seven days a week.
cards.source_title: The Table at Higgins | Campus Map - Clark University
cards.access_notes: Open daily; lunch typically starts at 11:15 AM or 12:00 PM depending on the day.

cards.title: Relax on the Campus Green
cards.subtitle: Friday Afternoon
cards.notes: Join fellow students on the central lawn for informal socializing. It is the heart of campus life and the site of major traditions like Spree Day.
cards.short_summary: The central outdoor gathering space at Clark University, ideal for meeting new friends between orientation sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: The Campus Green is a central location for student gatherings and major annual events like Spree Day.
cards.source_title: Campus Map | Clark University
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible outdoor space 24/7.

cards.title: Toast Marshmallows with New Friends
cards.subtitle: Saturday Night
cards.notes: Participate in evening orientation activities like marshmallow toasting. These events are designed to help first-year students bond in a relaxed setting.
cards.short_summary: A recurring orientation social activity where students gather at night to toast marshmallows and socialize.
cards.evidence_claim: Students toast marshmallows at night during one of the Saturday evening activities as part of the First-Year Experience.
cards.source_title: First-Year Experience | Clark University
cards.access_notes: Specific to orientation weekend; check your orientation schedule for exact times and locations.

cards.title: Brunch at a Neighborhood Staple
cards.subtitle: Sunday Morning
cards.notes: Visit this local diner for a mix of American breakfast and Salvadoran dishes. It occupies the historic space of the former Annie's Clark Brunch.
cards.short_summary: A beloved local diner near campus serving traditional brunch and Salvadoran specialties.
cards.evidence_claim: Belén's Clark Brunch opened at 934 Main St., taking over the longtime home of Annie's Clark Brunch near Clark University.
cards.source_title: New diner opens in longtime Annie's Clark Brunch location on Main Street
cards.access_notes: Open for breakfast and lunch; popular with students on weekends.

cards.title: Explore the Urban Forest
cards.subtitle: Sunday Afternoon
cards.notes: Take a 15-minute walk from campus to explore 26 acres of woodland trails. It is a peaceful spot for nature study and hiking in the city.
cards.short_summary: A 26-acre public green space owned by Clark University, featuring a network of trails and heritage trees.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hadwen Arboretum contains 26 acres of woodland green space and is a 15-minute walk from the main campus.
cards.source_title: Home | Hadwen Arboretum | Clark University
cards.access_notes: Open to the public daily from dawn to dusk.

cards.title: Swim or Work Out at the Kneller
cards.subtitle: Sunday Afternoon
cards.notes: Use your Clark ID to access the fitness center, basketball courts, or the six-lane swimming pool. It is the hub for campus recreation.
cards.short_summary: The primary athletic facility on campus, offering a pool, gym, and fitness center for student use.
cards.evidence_claim: The Kneller Athletic Center includes a gymnasium, the Bickman Fitness Center, and a six-lane, 25-yard swimming pool.
cards.source_title: Kneller Athletic Center | Campus Map | - Clark University
cards.access_notes: Requires a valid Clark ID for entry; check seasonal hours for the pool and fitness center.

cards.title: Find a Study Spot in the Library
cards.subtitle: Sunday Evening
cards.notes: Locate the Academic Commons on the second floor for group study or quiet research. The library is named after the father of modern rocketry.
cards.short_summary: The main university library, providing extensive study spaces and academic resources.
cards.evidence_claim: The Academic Commons at Goddard Library is a key academic hub; exterior doors are card-access 24/7 for students.
cards.source_title: Doors | Information Technology Services - Clark University
cards.access_notes: Exterior doors are card-access 24 hours a day for students with a Clark OneCard.

cards.title: Pick Up Clark Gear
cards.subtitle: Weekend Shopping
cards.notes: Located in the Shaich Family Alumni and Student Engagement Center, this is the place to buy Clark sweatshirts, gifts, and school supplies.
cards.short_summary: The official university bookstore and gift shop, owned and operated by Clark University.
cards.evidence_claim: The Clark University Campus Store is the source for Clark clothing, gifts, and supplies.
cards.source_title: Campus Store | Campus Map - Clark University
cards.access_notes: Open during standard business hours; check for special orientation weekend hours.

cards.title: Late Night Pizza and Subs
cards.subtitle: Weekend Late Night
cards.notes: Grab a hand-tossed pizza or a sub during late-night hours at the Higgins University Center. It is a popular spot for a midnight snack.
cards.short_summary: A late-night dining service offering pizza, subs, and snacks in the University Center.
cards.evidence_claim: Higgins Late Night operates Thursday through Saturday from 9:00 p.m. to 2:30 a.m., offering pizza and subs.
cards.source_title: Clark University | Dining Services - vbGraphics
cards.access_notes: Open late night Thursday-Saturday until 2:30 AM; accepts Clark Dining Dollars and cash.
